KNAVERY.Disclaimer: Base Knavery is an independent production of Dom Bosco and is not affiliated with Questing Beast LLC.
KNAVERY.DisclaimerShort: Base Knavery is an unofficial fan-made Foundry system for Knave (first and second editions) and is not affiliated with Questing Beast LLC.
KNAVERY.Knave1eCredit: The character traits, alignment, reaction, starting gear and the 100 level-less spells are from Knave (first edition) by Ben Milton, licensed under CC BY 4.0.
KNAVERY.LogoCredit: Knave: Second Edition is © Ben Milton and Questing Beast LLC. The “Made for Knave” logo is © Questing Beast LLC, used under the Knave: Second Edition Third Party License.
KNAVERY.Name: Name
KNAVERY.KindTip: Magic items, relics and potions get a badge on the Inventory row.
KNAVERY.EmployerTip: The character who hired them and pays their wage.
KNAVERY.WageTip: Coins a month (Knave 2e p59), or a day (Knave 1e's henchmen, p3).
KNAVERY.WagePeriodTip: Paid by the month or by the day.

Quality.Label: Quality
Quality.Tip: Knave 1e: what is left of the item's quality, and its full quality (blank for the usual: a weapon 3, a shield or helmet 1, body armor its armor points + 2). At 0 the item is destroyed and marked Broken.
Quality.Destroyed: {name} loses its last point of quality: destroyed, and marked Broken until repaired.
Quality.RepairTip: Knave 1e: each point of quality costs 10% of the item's price to repair. Paid from the owner's coins.
Quality.WearHint: A natural 20: the target's armor loses a point of quality. The target's owner picks the piece.
Quality.WearBody: A critical hit. Which piece of armor loses a point of quality?
Quality.NoArmor: {name} wears no armor that can lose quality.
Quality.RepairFreeTip: Mend this broken item. Knave 2e has no repair rule, so it costs nothing; the GM may ask for time or coins.

KNAVERY.BiographyPlaceholder: Click to write who this knave is, in 35 words or fewer.
KNAVERY.BackstoryTip: A good backstory is short: 35 words or fewer. Nothing stops a longer one.
KNAVERY.EffectModified: An Active Effect makes this {value} in play. The box holds the value without it.
KNAVERY.AbilityTip: Roll a {name} check: d20 + bonus. Its defense (what others must beat) is {defense}.
KNAVERY.DefenseTip: Defense: 11 + the bonus. An opposed check must reach this.

AbilityHint.STR: Melee attacks, lifting, climbing, breaking free
AbilityHint.WIS: Ranged attacks, foraging, navigation, spell resistance

AbilityHint1e.STR: Melee attacks, lifting, climbing, breaking free
AbilityHint1e.CON: Resisting poison and sickness, item slots, healing
AbilityHint1e.WIS: Ranged attacks, foraging, navigation, spotting illusions

KNAVERY.HPTip: Hit points. Damage comes off HP first; at 0 HP each further point is a wound.
KNAVERY.ACTip: Armor class: 11 + armor points ({ap}). Type a value to override it.
KNAVERY.ACAuto: AC = 11 plus 1 point for each piece of equipped armor.
KNAVERY.ACOverrideActive: Overridden by hand. Use the arrow to go back to the worn armor.
KNAVERY.ACReset: Go back to the armor you wear
KNAVERY.WoundsTip: Wounds fill item slots from the bottom up. Every slot wounded means death.
KNAVERY.CoinsTip: Coins. Every 100 (Knave 1e) or 500 (Knave 2e) fill an item slot, as the Rules say.
KNAVERY.NextLevelTip: XP needed for the next level.
KNAVERY.SlotsTip: Item slots: 10 + CON. Coins and wounds take slots too.
KNAVERY.RestTip: Rest for the night: HP back to full after two watches of sleep and a meal; a safe haven heals a wound too.
KNAVERY.RestHelp1e: A full night's rest after a meal heals d8 + CON. In a safe haven, all HP returns. Spellbooks are ready again either way.
KNAVERY.RestHelp: HP returns to full in the morning only after two watches of sleep and a meal the night before. In a safe haven, one wound heals as well. Spellbooks are ready again either way.
KNAVERY.RestAte: Ate a meal the night before

RestCard.Title: {name} rests for the night
RestCard.NoHp: No full night's sleep and meal: HP stays at {hp}.
RestCard.Haven1e: A safe haven: HP back to {max}.
RestCard.NoHp1e: No full night's rest after a meal: HP stays at {hp}.
RestCard.NoRations: No rations in the pack: the meal came from elsewhere, or there was none.

RulesSwitch.Title: Knave 2e rules?
RulesSwitch.Body: Your Knave 2e tables are built. Switch this world to Knave 2e rules?
RulesSwitch.Careers: Two careers and coins at creation
RulesSwitch.Wounds: Damage past 0 HP fills slots with wounds
RulesSwitch.Healing: Full HP after a night's sleep and a meal
RulesSwitch.Spells: As many spellbooks a day as INT
RulesSwitch.Attacks: A natural 1 breaks the weapon, and power attacks
RulesSwitch.Gear: Knave 2e prices and monthly wages, 500 coins to a slot
RulesSwitch.Advancement: Knave 2e XP (and XP for treasure), level-up HP and initiative
RulesSwitch.Characters: Characters you already have keep their numbers and items.
RulesSwitch.Done: This world now plays Knave 2e rules.

KNAVERY.HealWoundTip: Rest in a safe haven to heal one wound.
KNAVERY.WoundDown: Heal a wound (rest in a safe haven)
KNAVERY.DieOfFateTip: Roll a d6 when fate, not skill, should decide.
KNAVERY.LevelUpBody: Reaching level {level}. Choose {n} different abilities to raise by one, or let the dice choose.
KNAVERY.LevelUpHpKept: Rolled {rolled}, not above the old maximum: max HP is now {max}.
KNAVERY.LevelUpHpKeptBest: Rolled {rolled}, not above the old maximum: max HP stays {max}.
KNAVERY.LevelUpHpKeptLower: Rolled {rolled}, below the old maximum: max HP is now {max}.
KNAVERY.LevelUpArrow: Level Up: you have the XP for the next level

HpHint.Reroll: Max HP is rerolled with {formula}; if that is not above {max}, it becomes {next}.
HpHint.Best: Max HP is rerolled with {formula}, keeping the higher of the roll and {max}.
HpHint.Add: Max HP goes up by 1d6 from {max}.
HpHint.Knave1e: Max HP is rerolled with {formula}; if that is below {max}, it becomes {next}.

Initiative.Speaker: Initiative
Initiative.GmRolls: Initiative runs by side: the Game Master rolls for both sides.
Initiative.SurpriseFlavor: {surprised} are surprised. {acting} go first, with +5 to their combat checks for the round (add it yourself).

Growth.EachLevel: Each new level: +1 to {n} different abilities. {hp}

KNAVERY.GmNotesPlaceholder: Notes for this Knave's player. Only the Game Master can edit them.
KNAVERY.NoCareersHint: No careers. In Char Gen Mode, roll or pick them here, or drop a career item on the sheet.
KNAVERY.SecondCareer: Roll or pick the second career
KNAVERY.RollHp: Roll max HP for this level
KNAVERY.AbilityPointsTip: Level {level}: {max} points in all (3 at level 1, then +1 to three different abilities a level), and no ability above {cap}.
KNAVERY.RemoveCareerConfirm: Remove the career {name}, and the items it gave that are still carried?
KNAVERY.FeaturesHint: Fields this career adds to the character sheet. The key names where the value is stored.
KNAVERY.CareerKeyTip: A short id for storing this career's feature values. Leave blank to use the name.
KNAVERY.StartingItemsHint: Type an item name and press Enter, or drop an item here.
KNAVERY.EffectsHint: Active Effects on a career apply to whoever holds it, e.g. +1 to max HP.
KNAVERY.CreationModeHintOn: Char Gen Mode is on: dice and pick-lists appear, abilities can be edited, the marketplace lets you take gear, and Level Up shows when you have the XP.
KNAVERY.CreationModeHintOff: Turn on Char Gen Mode to edit abilities, reroll parts of the sheet and level up.

Hint.monster: From the bestiary, with its HP rolled.
Hint.person: Someone met on the road: a random name, traits and portrait.
Hint.hireling: A hireling, mercenary or expert, with their wage.
Hint.companion: Travels with a knave: a half share of XP, no morale tests.

Npc.NoBestiary: The bestiary compendium is empty or missing.

KNAVERY.ImprovisedHint: A fist, a rock, a chair leg: d4, STR, no slot.
KNAVERY.NoAttacks: No equipped weapon. Equip one in the Inventory.
KNAVERY.AttackTip: Attack: d20 + STR (melee) or WIS (ranged) against the target's AC (Knave 1e: it must beat it).
KNAVERY.TreasureTip: Loot brought back from a dungeon: the XP tab counts it once for XP (when the Rules give XP for treasure), and it sells for its full value.

Party.Overloaded: Carrying more than their slots: overloaded

SpellGen.Title: Generate a spell
SpellGen.Reroll: Roll this word again (one word only)
SpellGen.RerollUsed: One word has been rolled again already
SpellGen.Name: The spell's name
SpellGen.Hint: Adjust the wording if you like. The spell's effect is yours and the GM's to agree.
SpellGen.Missing: Generating a spell needs these tables, built from the Knave 2e book: {names}. The GM builds them on the dashboard's Tables tab, or imports them.
SpellGen.CardBody: {name} adds it as a spellbook. Its effect is for the player and the GM to agree.

Sell.Hint: Sell this: half its price, or its full value for treasure
Sell.Title: Sell {name}
Sell.PriceTreasure: {n} × {name} sells for {price}c, its full value as treasure.
Sell.HalfHint: A shop pays half an item's price.
Sell.TreasureHint: Treasure sells for its full value.

KNAVERY.UnusableTip: A wound fills this slot: the item can't be used until the wound heals. Whether it was dropped or broken is the table's call.
KNAVERY.SpellsLeftTip: Each spellbook can be used once a day, and you can use as many a day as your INT.
KNAVERY.SlotIndexTip: The slot or slots this item sits in. Wounds fill slots from the bottom.
KNAVERY.ReorderHint: Drag rows to reorder. The bottom rows are wounded and marked unusable or damaged first.
KNAVERY.BundleTip: How many of these share one slot (e.g. 20 arrows).

Status.UnconsciousText: At 0 HP. Any more damage kills.
Status.NoHpText: Further damage fills slots with wounds.
Status.WoundedText: Items in wounded slots are unusable until the wounds heal.

KNAVERY.MoraleTip: Morale: roll 2d6; at or under MRL they stand firm.
KNAVERY.NpcACTip: Armor class. Worn armor adds to it.
KNAVERY.NpcLevelTip: Level: the bonus this creature adds to every check and attack.
KNAVERY.NpcCheckTip: A check with the creature's level as its bonus.
KNAVERY.NpcUsesLevel: Adds its level (+{n}) to every check.

Roll.TipDis2d20: Roll two d20s and keep the lower
Roll.TipAdv2d20: Roll two d20s and keep the higher
Roll.RollDamageToo: Roll damage at the same time
Roll.IdealWeaponHint: Knave 1e: the right weapon for this foe adds a damage die (the GM says).
Roll.RangedHint: Ranged: not while in melee; −5 if the target is in melee (Knave 2e).
Roll.PowerAttackHint: Double the damage dice. The weapon breaks.
Roll.PowerAttackUsed: Power attack: double damage dice, and the weapon breaks.
Roll.FreeManeuver: 21 or more: a free maneuver as well.
Roll.Natural20: A natural 20: a critical hit. One more damage die, and the target's armor loses a point of quality.
Roll.ApplyHint: Apply to the hit targets, or to your targeted or selected tokens.
Roll.ApplyDirectHint: Direct damage skips HP and wounds a character at once; a creature takes it tripled.
Roll.AppliedAgain: This damage has already been applied. Apply it again?

Damage.Title: {name} takes {n} damage
Damage.DropWounded: Items in wounded slots are unusable until the wounds heal.

Spell.ChaosNote: A chaos spellbook: it becomes a different spell at the next dawn.
Spell.DailyLimit: You can only use {n} spellbooks per day.
Spell.DailyLimitOne: You can only use {n} spellbook per day.
Spell.LevelHint: Up to your INT. The level sets the spell's power and its save.
Spell.Save2e: A target of higher level may check against {target}: a success halves the effect, 10 over ends it.
Spell.Save1e: An unwilling target may save: INT against level {level}.

Carousing.Title: Carousing
Carousing.Help: The night costs d10 × 50c (village), × 100c (town) or × 200c (city) and earns as many XP as it cost. Next morning: a CON check, with a mishap on a failure.
Carousing.Spent: {name} caroused in a {where}: {rolled}c called for, {spent}c spent, {spent} XP gained.
Carousing.NoTable: No Carousing Mishaps table yet: build it from your book on the Tables page.

Hint.encounter: Roll the area's encounter table, then its reaction and distance.
Hint.fatigue: Everyone takes 1 damage, except those who rest through the next turn or watch.
Hint.depletion: Each ration, or other food that spoils, is rolled on a d6 and spoils on a 1.
Hint.burn: Each lit torch is used up.
Hint.shift: The weather turns, or something in the area changes.
Hint.sign: A clue: tracks, a sound or a smell that hints at something close by or hidden.

Hazard.ForcedMarch: More than three watches of travel today: each traveller takes 1 direct damage unless they pass a CON check.

MoraleTest.AloneHalfHp: {name} stands alone, at half HP or less.
MoraleTest.RallyHelp: If the leader passes a CHA check, {name} rolls morale again. Each side may try once a battle.
MoraleTest.RallyUsed: This side has already tried to rally this battle.
MoraleTest.NoRally1e: Knave 1e has no rally: a failed morale test stands.
MoraleTest.Companion: {name} is a companion: companions never test morale.

Wages.Title: Wages
Wages.None: No hirelings with a wage. Create NPC makes them, and a hireling's sheet names who pays.
Wages.NeedEmployer: Choose an employer on the hireling's sheet first.
Wages.ChooseEmployer: Choose who employs {name} on their sheet first.
Wages.CannotPay: {name} has {coins}c, not the {wage}c the wage needs.
Wages.Paid: {employer} paid {name} {wage}c: wages for the next {days} days.

Time.Resting: The party is resting (fatigue is ignored)
Time.Travelling: Travelling this watch (counts toward the day's three)
Time.ForageHelp: A watch spent looking for food: a WIS check for d6 rations. The watch then ends and the hazard die rolls.
Time.DungeonHint: Ending a turn moves the world clock on 10 minutes and rolls the dungeon hazard die. Fatigue, burn and depletion cards carry a button: nothing changes until you click it.
Time.TravelHint: Ending a watch moves the world clock on 4 hours and rolls the travel hazard die. A day has six watches. Fatigue and depletion cards carry a button: nothing changes until you click it.
Time.FatigueHelp: Untick anyone who will rest through the next turn or watch. The others take 1 damage.

Offer.NoTargets: There is nobody to give it to.
Offer.OverburdenBody: {target} has no free slot for {item}. Take it anyway?
Offer.GiverOffline: {giver}'s player is offline; the offer waits for them.
Offer.Failed: The hand-over failed; the offer is open again.

Refused.Answered: That offer has already been answered.
Refused.Busy: That offer is being handed over right now.

Market.Title: Marketplace: {name}
Market.TakeHint: Take it without paying (the Game Master, or Char Gen Mode).
Market.ManagerHint: Aisles are roll tables named "Market: …" (Knave 2e prices) or "Market 1e: …" (Knave 1e prices); the page shows the world's price list. Shipped aisles are read-only: Customize makes a world copy that replaces them.
Market.DeleteAisleConfirm: Delete the aisle {name}? A shipped aisle of the same name comes back.
Market.ShippedHint: Ships with the system. Customize it to change prices or stock.
Market.Customized: {name} is now a world aisle you can edit.
Market.CustomizeFirst: Customize this aisle first; shipped aisles are read-only.
Market.DropHint: Drop items here to stock them.

ItemMaker.Title: Create Item

Hint.weapon: A die by its hands and reach; under Knave 1e attacks, its quality.
Hint.armor: A piece of armor: its type and points.
Hint.gear: An ordinary item: one slot, a price band.
Hint.potion: One dose, with the potion badge.
Hint.relic: A singular thing, with the relic badge.
Hint.spellbook: A spellbook; Roll names its spell from your spell tables.
Hint.chaos: A spellbook whose spell changes at the dawn after a casting.

ItemMaker.ChaosNote: Chaos: its spell changes at the dawn after it is cast. The swap is yours to make.
ItemMaker.WhereAisles: A marketplace aisle (the item also goes in the Items directory)
ItemMaker.NoAisles: No world aisle yet: Customize a shipped aisle, or add one, on the dashboard’s Marketplace page
ItemMaker.RollMissing: Needs {tables}: build from your book on the dashboard’s Tables tab, or import.
ItemMaker.MadeAisle: {name} is on the {where} aisle, and in the Items directory.
ItemMaker.NoTarget: That actor or aisle is gone. Choose again.

Dashboard.Title: Game Master's Dashboard
Dashboard.YoursFolder: Yours is the folder {folder} in your user data ({count} images).
Dashboard.YoursFolderOne: Yours is the folder {folder} in your user data (one image).
Dashboard.XpHint: Award XP to the players' characters: the same to each, a different amount to each, a total split evenly, or (when the Rules give XP for treasure) the treasure they brought back.
Dashboard.TreasureHintCoin: 1 XP per coin of treasure recovered from a dungeon and brought back to civilization, split evenly among the characters who helped; a companion takes a half share. Tick who helped: their treasure is listed, and each item counts once.
Dashboard.TreasureHintGold: Knave 1e, XP for gold: 1 XP per 100 copper of treasure brought back, split evenly among the characters who helped; a companion takes a half share. Tick who helped: their treasure is listed, and each item counts once.
Dashboard.TreasureTotalCompanions: Treasure worth {coins}c: {xp} XP, split among {n} and {companions} companion(s) at a half share.
Dashboard.TreasureNothing: Nothing to award: tick who helped, and the treasure or coins they brought back.
Dashboard.XpCardCompanion: {name} (companion, half share): {xp} XP. Note it on their sheet.
Dashboard.XpNothing: Nothing to award: choose characters and an amount.
Dashboard.ReasonHint: What the players see, e.g. "The floor gives way!"
Dashboard.DifficultyCreature: Against a creature: its matching ability score, or its level if it has none.
Dashboard.DifficultyEdge: Easier or harder because of the situation? Set the edge instead.
Dashboard.DamageHint: Roll damage and apply it, the Knave way: HP first, then wounds.
Dashboard.CombatNotStarted: No fight is running. Add tokens to the Combat Tracker and press Begin Combat.
Dashboard.RollInitiativeTip: Knave 1e: one d6 for the round. Knave 2e: the leaders' CHA check. Individual: everyone rolls.
Dashboard.SurpriseTip2: Round 1 goes to the side that surprised, with +5 to its combat checks for the round.
Dashboard.LeadersHint: The leaders make the CHA check that decides who acts first. Left alone: the party's highest CHA and the enemies' highest level.
Dashboard.HazardPresetNone: Type a formula, or pick a hazard

Hazards.freezing: Freezing (1 a turn, direct; a CON check avoids it)

Dashboard.HazardDiceHint: Rolls the die only. The Time page's End turn / End watch also moves the clock on.
Dashboard.SurpriseTip: For a meeting within 80' (Knave 2e p19). Sets up the check on the Requests page: the nearest PC's WIS, with the nearest creature's WIS as the difficulty; a margin of 5 or more means surprise. Tick that PC, type the creature's WIS, and send.
Dashboard.SurpriseReason: Surprise! The closest PC: WIS against the closest creature's WIS. Win by 5 or more to surprise them; lose by 5 or more and you are surprised.
Dashboard.QuickNpcTip: A name, a personality, a profession and a detail, from the tables your world has (pp54-57). Create NPC makes a full one.
Dashboard.QuickNpcMissing: A quick NPC needs at least one of Names, Personalities, Professions or NPC Details: build them on the Tables page from your Knave 2e book, or import them.
Dashboard.SelectNpcs: Select the NPC tokens that test morale.
Dashboard.DiceHint: These rolls are whispered to you.
Dashboard.EventsHint: From the tables built from your Knave 2e book (Tables page), or imported by name.
Dashboard.EventMissing: Build the {name} table first: on the Tables page, from your Knave 2e book, or import it.
Dashboard.TablesHint: Shipped tables are empty shells. Import your own rows; the world copy is used from then on.

Import.Title: Import a table
Import.Intro: Paste rows to create or replace a world table. A world table overrides the shipped shell of the same name.
Import.Formats: One row per line. Ranges like "01-05" or "7." are kept; plain lines are numbered in order. Careers: "Name: item, item, item" gives starting items. Link a document with @UUID[…]{Name}.
Import.Failed: Importing into {name} failed, and the table was left as it was. See the browser console.
Import.Unlinked: Rows whose @UUID link named no document were imported as plain text: {n}.

Gen.LowestBody: Each score is the lowest of three d6. You may swap two of them.
Gen.RandomHint: Rolled stats, careers, coins, portrait, etc.
Gen.BlankHint: An empty sheet for building your character yourself.
Gen.RerollConfirm: Reroll {name} from scratch? Items and careers are replaced.
Gen.PointsBody: Place {n} points in your abilities. At first level only, more than one may go in the same ability. Everything else is rolled.
Gen.NoCareerTable: The Careers table is empty; pick careers by hand.
Gen.NoSpellTable: The Spells table is empty; no spellbooks rolled.

Art.UrlPlaceholder: …or paste an image path or URL
Art.SourceEmpty: {gallery} has no portraits to roll; rolling from every gallery that is on.
Art.CustomEmpty: Put images in the "{folder}" folder of your user data, then rescan.

Notify.RandomizationDisabled: The Game Master has turned off Char Gen Mode for players.
Notify.TwoCareers: A knave has two careers. Change one on the Growth page.
Notify.AbilityBudget: At level {level} a knave has {max} ability points in all; {n} were left to place.
Notify.AbilityCap: At level {level} no ability can be above {cap}.
Notify.CareersLocked: Careers change only at level 1, in Char Gen Mode (the Game Master can always change them).
Notify.FieldLocked: That needs Char Gen Mode on (and, for level and XP, the Game Master's permission).
Notify.CreationClosed: The Game Master has turned off character creation.
Notify.CreationRequested: Asked the Game Master to create your character.
Notify.NoGmForCreation: A Game Master must be online to create your character.
Notify.NoGmForDamage: A Game Master must be online to damage tokens you don't own.
Notify.TableEmpty: The "{name}" table is still empty. The Game Master can import rows from the dashboard.
Notify.MarketplaceEmpty: The marketplace has nothing for sale.
Notify.Overburdened: {name} is carrying more than they have slots for.
Notify.NoCareers: No careers found. Import the Careers table or create career items.
Notify.NotEnoughXp: Not enough XP for the next level yet.
Notify.PickThree: Choose {n} different abilities, or press Random.
Notify.PrintBlocked: The browser blocked the print window. Allow pop-ups for this site.
Notify.NpcRollManual: NPCs aren't rolled; drop stats in from the bestiary.
Notify.GmOnly: Only the Game Master can do that.
Notify.NotADamageFormula: "{formula}" is not a dice formula, so no damage was rolled.
Notify.EmbeddedStartingItem: That item belongs to an actor in a compendium. Drag it from the Items sidebar or an Items compendium instead.
Notify.NoSettingsPermission: Your user may not change world settings (core permission: Modify Configuration Settings).
Notify.PurchaseFailed: The purchase did not go through, and no coins were taken. See the browser console.
Notify.CreationFailed: The Game Master's client could not create your character. Ask the Game Master to try again.

Settings.GroupGeneralHint: Rolls, traits, the change log and the welcome window.
Settings.GroupGenerationHint: Who may create characters and change level or XP; starting levels; your portraits.
Settings.GroupInventoryHint: The players' marketplace, coin slots, rations and torches.
Settings.GroupHacksHint: Knave 1e, Knave 2e or a mix of the two.
Settings.RulesHint: Sets every rule below to one edition. Change any one to mix.

CreationAbilitiesChoice.lowest: Knave 1e: lowest of 3d6 each, swap two

StartingKitChoice.knave1e: Knave 1e: rolled gear and a weapon of choice

Settings.HealingRuleHint: A safe haven: all HP (1e), one wound (2e).

HealingRuleChoice.knave1e: Knave 1e: d8 + CON after a meal
HealingRuleChoice.knave2e: Knave 2e: all HP after sleep and a meal

SpellRuleChoice.book-per-day: Knave 1e: each book once a day
SpellRuleChoice.int-per-day: Knave 2e: INT casts, each book once

Settings.AttackRuleHint: 1e: a 20 adds a damage die and wears armor, a 1 wears the weapon. 2e: a 1 breaks the weapon; free maneuver at 21+.
Settings.CoinsPerSlotHint: Only while Coins take slots (Inventory) is on.
Settings.GroupRulebookHint: Your own Knave 2e PDF, read inside Foundry.
Settings.GroupPrintingHint: The paper, the text size and what the printed sheet carries.
Settings.WeaponBreaksHint: Knave 2e attacks only; under Knave 1e a 1 costs quality.
Settings.ShowTraitsHint: The traits on the Description page.
Settings.ChangeLogHint: Whispers you a card when someone edits a sheet by hand.
Settings.WelcomeOnStartHint: Opens for the GM at every login and refresh. Players never see it.
Settings.AllowPlayerRandomization: Players may use Char Gen Mode
Settings.AllowPlayerRandomizationHint: Editing abilities, the dice and pick-lists, Roll Character and Level Up.
Settings.AllowPlayerLevelXpHint: In Char Gen Mode. Off, only the GM may; Level Up still works.
Settings.FirstLevelHpHint: Under a reroll rule, also the reroll's first die.
Settings.TreasureXpHint: Awarded on the dashboard's XP page. XP for gold is 1e's designer's note.

InitiativeChoice.1e-d6: Knave 1e: one d6 a round, by side
InitiativeChoice.2e-leaders: Knave 2e: the leaders' CHA check, by side

Settings.Knave1eAlignmentHint: On the Knave page, rolled for new characters.
Settings.Knave1eBackgroundHint: On the Knave page, rolled for new characters.
Settings.Knave1eStartingGearHint: Random creation also rolls Knave 1e's starting gear: armor, helmet and shield, two dungeoneering items and two general items.
Settings.SpellListHint: Knave 1e's spells ship with the system (L = caster level). A built or imported Spells table takes over unless you choose Knave 1e.
Settings.CustomPortraitFolderHint: Its images come first in the portrait picker and in random portraits.
Settings.AllowPlayerMarketplaceHint: Shows the Marketplace button on character sheets.
Settings.CoinsTakeSlotsHint: As many to a slot as Coins per slot (Rules) says.
Settings.RationsPerSlotHint: Days of rations in one slot. Both editions: 1.
Settings.TorchesPerSlotHint: Torches in one slot. Knave 1e's gear table bundles 5.
Settings.HardModeWoundsHint: An item in a wounded slot breaks.
Settings.PrintPaperHint: The printed sheet fits A4 and US Letter alike; Auto leaves the paper to the print dialog.
Settings.PrintTextSizeHint: The printed sheet's body text. One page at either size.
Settings.PrintCareerFeaturesHint: Prints each career's features (Knave 2e); its description stays on the career.
Settings.PrintBackstoryHint: Prints the backstory, six lines at most.
Settings.PrintNotesLinesHint: Pencil lines fill the room left under the notes.
Settings.RulebookPdfHint: Choose from this computer uploads your copy to the server's knavery-rulebook folder; the folder button picks one already there. Only the path is stored; anyone logged in who knows the address can fetch the file.
Settings.RulebookForPlayersHint: Players get the reader and you can show them a page. Off hides the reader; the file stays reachable.
Settings.RulebookPageOffsetHint: PDF page minus printed page. In the Knave 2e PDF, printed page 1 is PDF page 7: offset 6.

Rulebook.Title: Rulebook
Rulebook.KeyHint: Toggles the reader on your own copy of the rulebook.
Rulebook.NobodyToShow: Nobody to show: no player is connected, or players may not read the rulebook (Configure Rulebook).
Rulebook.NotSet: No rulebook PDF is set for this world. Choose your copy from your computer on the dashboard's Tables tab or in Configure Rulebook.
Rulebook.UploadFailed: The rulebook could not be uploaded. See the browser console.

RulebookTables.Intro: These are the tables read from your copy of the book. Open one to check or correct its rows (one per line, as the table importer reads them), untick any you do not want, then build. They become world roll tables in the From your rulebook folder; the system rolls on Careers, Spells, Names, Surnames and Reaction at once. A table you made or edited yourself is never overwritten.

Welcome.Title: Welcome to Base Knavery
Welcome.Unofficial: Base Knavery is an unofficial, fan-made Foundry VTT system for Knave, first and second editions.
Welcome.NotEndorsed: Questing Beast LLC did not make it and has not endorsed it.
Welcome.Rules1eBody: A new world plays Ben Milton's original Knave as written. Its rules, tables and spells come with the system.
Welcome.Rules2eTitle: Knave 2e relies on your purchased copy of the book.
Welcome.Rules2eBody: Upload your Knave 2e PDF and build its tables, and you'll be offered a switch to 2e rules. Characters you already have don't change.
Welcome.RulesMixBody: Each rule has its own switch in Game Settings, under Configure Rules.
Welcome.Author: Both editions of Knave were written by Ben Milton.
Welcome.Book1eNote: Its rules are already in the system. Buying the PDF supports its author.
Welcome.Knave1eBody: The Knave rules, traits, alignment, reaction, starting gear, price list and the 100 level-less spells come from Knave by Ben Milton, licensed under {license}. Changes: the rules set out as Foundry automation and settings, the tables as roll tables, the price list as items and shop aisles with one item per weapon, 1e armor as armor points, and "Misfortunes" named Misfortune. A table you build from your Knave 2e book replaces its 1e counterpart.
Welcome.PortraitAlt: A knave, drawn by Lydia Comer
Welcome.Knave2eHeading: Knave: Second Edition Third Party License
Welcome.NoAiArtBody: Base Knavery ships with more than 2,900 human-made art assets (portraits, tokens and icons) and will never use AI-generated art.
Welcome.NoAiTextBody: No spell, item or monster description was written by AI.
Welcome.AiCode: Base Knavery's code is written with the help of an AI coding assistant.
Welcome.ChooseRulebook: Choose your rulebook PDF from this computer
Welcome.NoRulebook: Playing Knave 2e? Upload your Knave 2e PDF to read it in Foundry and build its tables. It is uploaded to this server only.
